title: Spaces which "partial download files" occupies on Desktop must always be available for any other file type to seamlessly take its place.
line: Files downloaded to the desktop no longer leave empty gaps where their partial download files used to be.
explanation: Firefox creates name.part and an empty name placeholder, then renames the .part over the placeholder when the download ends; Chromium renames a .crdownload file. Folder View gave each new file the first free desktop slot, so when the .part file was created first it took the earlier slot and left a hole once it vanished. With several downloads the desktop ended up with a gap after every file. Now, whenever a regular file is placed, it takes the earliest slot held by a partial download (.part, .crdownload, .partial, .download, .opdownload, .!qB, .!ut) and that partial file moves to the new file's slot, so partial downloads always trail and leave no gaps.

commits.message:
Positioner: place new files before partial downloads

Browsers create a partial download file before or next to the final one,
so its spot on the desktop turned into a gap once the download finished.
New items now take the earliest spot held by a partial download instead.

BUG: 495319

media.caption: Three Firefox-style downloads in progress: each .part file took the slot before its final file

Same downloads with the fix: final files come first, .part files are pushed to the end
